doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Diversatonic and respecting differences
summary: His upcoming organ-flavored record Diversatonic and his plea to respect one another.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: Well we’ve been at this for about an hour, it’s been wonderful.
Oh my goodness. I’m going to let you talk next time.

I’m wondering if you have anything to say about the state of our country. Because you are an observer of human nature, and you were just talking about extremes. Do you have anything you can comment on?

Well my current mission man, my current thought and my current project, and it’s more, I’ve got a record coming out in April. I did it here locally in Durham you know. And with guys I didn’t really know that well. I brought in a ringer from New York, an organ player by the name of Kyle Kohler. ‘Cause I played with all of the great organ players. I probably played with more great organ player than anybody on the planet. Jimmy Smith, Jimmy McGriff, you can’t name but maybe two organ players that I didn’t play with. So I never made an organ record. This is sort of a record with an organ vibe on it. But the name of it is “Diversatonic” “Diversatonic.” And it’s inspired by what’s going on now and the truth is [gap] stop, man, like worrying about the fact that we’re all different man.

Because we are and that’s a fact of life. Man, we’re all different and you know we should just respect each other for our differences and naturally we don’t have to all agree but we have to respect each other or else we’re headed toward self-destruction. The fact is simple. It’s simple. You know the best way to get some respect is to die, and then everybody be [groans] everybody is interested in you then. But no, respect the living you know, because it’s important and we’d have such a better, better world and you know, be concerned with your fellow man. We certainly have enough on earth to go around but yet we have people in terrible shape. And it’s been that way since the beginning of time. So life itself and humanity should be about self-improvement. In other words, the goal today is to be better than you were yesterday. And that does not mean — it takes work but it’s very important. Why would you want to be worse today, you know, unless things had to get sick and so and so, yes. But spiritually, psychologically, you have to keep trying to be better. Cut me off because I’m on a ramble.
